transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Ethan Li (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Cumulus Head of ML), Marcus Ruiz (Platform Eng), Lena Hoffman (CTO)
Recording id: ff-20251120-cumulus-001

Optional auto sections:
Summary: align on POC success criteria (latency/throughput), propose reserved GPU sizing and burst policy, plan benchmarks and timelines.
Topics: Success criteria; workload sizing; reserved vs burst capacity; fallback policies to hosted/quantized variants; benchmark plan and timeline.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro - I'm Samira, AE at Redwood, and Ethan our SE is with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Priya: Good, thanks. we've been trying to scope a POC to move some of our chat and summarization traffic off our current infra and test dedicated inference.
[00:20] Marcus: yeah, we've got a mix of T4s and a couple of A100s in our k8s cluster, but it's messy, autoscaling is manual, and cost is all over the place.
[00:30] Ethan: got it. that's a pretty common starting point. today we'd like to align on success criteria for the POC, figure out initial reserved GPU sizing, and talk about a burst / fallback strategy so you don't hit 503s if load spikes.
[00:45] Lena: timeline wise, we want to validate within 3-4 weeks and if that looks good, move to a 90-day pilot.
[00:52] Samira: perfect. let's start with success criteria  Priya, what's the user-facing SLA you care about? p95 latency, tokens per response, anything else?
[01:05] Priya: p95 latency < 600ms for chat flows (avg prompt 150 tokens, response ~60 tokens). for batch summarization throughput we want ~200 requests/minute with eventual consistency on lower priority jobs. cost target is a softer constraint  need to be below our current on-prem unit cost.
[01:25] Ethan: okay that's helpful. for planning we usually translate that to target tokens/sec and concurrency. with 150+60 token exchanges, that maps to roughly X tokens/sec at your target RPS  if you want we can compute exact tokens/sec after we get traces.
[01:40] Marcus: we can provide traces  we have 7 days of request logs and token histograms.
[01:45] Samira: great. on the capacity side, two levers: reserved GPUs (predictable throughput + isolation) and burst/overflow capacity using our shared pools or routing to hosted models. initial proposal would be 4 reserved A100-equivalent slots with burst up to 8 for spikes.
[02:05] Priya: 4 A100s seems like a heavy lift cost-wise. any less heavy option?
[02:12] Ethan: you can mix  start with 2 reserved A100s plus 2 reserved A40/T4 equivalents for lower priority traffic, and let burst cover transient peaks. also we can use quantized int8 model variants for burst/fallback which increases throughput ~1.8-2x at a small quality delta.
[02:30] Lena: is quantization automatic? i.e., will we lose accuracy?
[02:34] Ethan: good question, it's model-dependent. we run calibrated quantaization profiles  excuse me, quantaization  to measure quality delta. for many LLMs the customer impact is minimal on non-sensitive summarization, but for chat you might want to keep a higher fidelity variant for 100% of traffic and only route low-priority or bulk jobs to the quantized variant.
[02:55] Marcus: how does failover work if the reserved pool is saturated? do we see 503s or do requests get queued?
[03:02] Samira: we recommend a multi-tier fallback policy: 1) automatic overflow to Redwood shared burst pool (if enabled) 2) if burst capacity not available, route to a quantized model variant in the same region, 3) as a last resort, fallback to our hosted API with degraded SLOs but guaranteed availability. all of this is configurable per-route.
[03:25] Priya: what about data residency / VPC constraints? we need to keep everything in our VPC for this pilot.
[03:32] Ethan: for Private deployments we support a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC and can run Dedicated pools inside your network. for the POC we can run the control plane in your VPC and still offer burst via secure peering to Redwood shared capacity if you opt-in  otherwise burst would be to your own extra nodes.
[03:52] Lena: ok quick note  SOC2 and KMS/audit logs are hard requirements.
[03:57] Samira: absolutely. we'll share our SOC2 report and KMS integration docs in the follow-up.
[04:03] Ethan: turning back to benchmarks  our suggested plan: 1) warm-up phase (30m) to populate KV cache 2) steady-state perf run (2h) with traffic replayed from your traces at 1x and 2x load 3) targeted p95/p99 measurements and memory profiling. we'll also include token-level cost metrics.
[04:25] Marcus: i want to make sure KV cache behavior is represented  your caching for prefix reuse is a big win for us. how do you measure cache hit rates?
[04:34] Ethan: we export cache-hit metrics per-route; typical test includes synthetic replay of repeated prompts to measure prefix reuse and hit ratios. warmup helps reach realistic hit rates. note that transcriptions sometimes call it "K-V cash" in our logs, so sorry for any odd terms.
[04:50] Priya: what about autoscale thresholds? like when do you spin up more nodes, and how fast?
[04:56] Ethan: autoscale is policy driven  you can set target CPU/GPU utilization or request queue length. for GPU-backed models we scale at defined capacity granularity (e.g., 1 GPU step) and use fast spin-up for burst (pre-warmed standbys) to reduce spin-up time. we typically recommend pre-warming 1-2 nodes for expected peaks, and using burst for short spikes.
[05:18] Samira: practically, for the POC we'll propose two configs: conservative (2 A100 + 2 lower-tier reserved, burst to 6) and aggressive (4 A100 reserved, burst to 8). we'll include pricing and expected throughput for both so you can pick.
[05:32] Marcus: can you show expected p95 numbers for our median payload?
[05:36] Ethan: we can give model-level perf estimates; they'll be approximate until we run your traces. for example, a single A100 can serve approx N tokens/sec for the model family you're interested in  we'll calculate exact numbers in the sizing doc.
[05:50] Priya: also want canary rollout behavior  we need to be able to run 10% traffic to new model variant then ramp.
[05:55] Samira: yes rollouts/canary is supported, with automatic rollback on quality regressions if you hook up eval metrics. we'll include a recommended rollout plan in the POC doc.
[06:05] Lena: logging and tracing  we need per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdown.
[06:10] Ethan: included. Redwood Console gives per-route token breakdowns, latency histograms, and trace IDs you can correlate with your logs.
[06:18] Priya: any known limitations for multi-tenant burst? we want isolation for PII workloads.
[06:24] Samira: for PII/regulatory you should run Dedicated in your VPC or our Private offering. burst to shared pools is available only if you opt-in and don't require strict data residency. we'll annotate that in the doc.
[06:40] Marcus: for the benchmark run, what's the timeline to schedule?
[06:44] Samira: if you send traces by Friday (2025-11-21) we can schedule a 2-hour run the week of 2025-11-24. we'll need a day to prep staging and warm caches.
[06:54] Priya: ok we'll get traces to you.
[06:58] Ethan: on the actual test, we'll run a warmup to populate KV cache, then a steady run at 1x load for 1 hour and a spike window for 30 minutes at 2x, plus a teardown. we'll capture p50/p95/p99 and token costs.
[07:12] Lena: one last question  in case of model mismatch or quality drop during canary, do you support automatic fallback per user session?
[07:18] Ethan: yes, we support per-route and per-session fallback. you can configure session affinity so a user's session remains on the higher-fidelity variant; if quality drops, you can either rollback or route to a different model variant automatically.
[07:30] Samira: great. recap of next steps: Samira to send sizing/pricing, Ethan to send benchmark plan + scripts, Priya to share traces and token histograms, schedule benchmark for next week.
[07:44] Priya: sounds good, thanks.
[07:47] Samira: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc and link to SOC2/security pack.
[07:52] (call ends)

Notes: Transcript contains some auto-transcription artifacts ("K-V cash" for KV cache, "quantaization" for quantization). References to exact tokens/sec or GPU performance will be calculated after Redwood analyzes the provided traces.
